name: Stanford Research Institute

summary.text: Stanford Research Institute was founded on October 24, 1946 by Stanford University's trustees as a nonprofit research organization in Menlo Park, California. It separated from Stanford in 1970, after student protests over its Defense Department-funded work, and was renamed SRI International in 1977. Douglas Engelbart's Augmentation Research Center at SRI, funded from 1963, built the NLS system and hosted the second node of the ARPANET in 1969; SRI also ran the ARPANET Network Information Center. A 1968 SRI report for the American Petroleum Institute by Elmer Robinson and R.C. Robbins warned that rising carbon dioxide could produce noticeable temperature increases.

facts.claim: Stanford Research Institute was founded on October 24, 1946, after plans had been shelved during the Depression and the Second World War; research chemist William F. Talbot was its first director.
facts.quote: Founded on October 24, 1946, Stanford Research Institute was the convergence of two parallel efforts in California

facts.claim: SRI formally separated from Stanford University in 1970 and became SRI International in 1977. The separation followed student protests during the Vietnam War by protesters who believed SRI's DARPA-funded work was making the university part of the military-industrial complex.
facts.quote: SRI formally separated from Stanford University in 1970 and, in 1977, became known as SRI International.

facts.claim: In 1963 Douglas Engelbart began receiving funds for his own research laboratory at SRI, the Augmented Human Intellect Research Center, later shortened to the Augmentation Research Center (ARC), whose NLS system is described as a forerunner of office automation and personal computing environments.
facts.quote: in 1963, he began to receive funds for his own research laboratory at SRI which was called the Augmented Human Intellect Research Center (AHIRC), later shortened to Augmentation Research Center (ARC)

facts.claim: SRI's own account says Engelbart's group provided the second node of the ARPANET: the first message was attempted from UCLA to SRI on October 29, 1969 and crashed after part of the word was transmitted; the UCLA-SRI link was firmly established on November 21, 1969, and by December 5, 1969 UC Santa Barbara and the University of Utah were added to form a four-node network.
facts.quote: the ARPANET link between UCLA and SRI was firmly established on November 21, 1969

facts.claim: The ARPANET Network Information Center, located at SRI in Menlo Park, was the first NIC (1970); in 1973 it was spun off as a separate project with Elizabeth Feinler as principal investigator.
facts.quote: the Arpanet Network Information Center, located at SRI in Menlo Park, CA, was the first NIC (1970)

facts.claim: Inside Climate News reported in 2016 that the 1968 SRI report for API called carbon dioxide 'the only air pollutant which has been proven to be of global importance to man's environment on the basis of a long period of scientific investigation' and warned that if CO2 levels continued to rise at present rates, noticeable increases in temperature could occur. It also reported that a January 1972 API Committee for Air and Water Conservation status report acknowledged the SRI report.
facts.quote: If CO2 levels continue to rise at present rates, it is likely that noticeable increases in temperature could occur

openQuestions: Site claim (Carbon Ledger): the SRI report for API says significant temperature changes are 'almost certain to occur by the year 2000'. Inside Climate News and DeSmog summarize the report with similar wording; the report's full text was not opened, and the site currently cites Wikipedia for this item.
Site claim (Crash Conduits): by 1971 DARPA 'deliberately divested the network to private contractors without retaining public royalties'. No source for this characterization was found.
The SRI account gives the host as an 'SDS-90' while other sources name the SDS 940; the discrepancy was not resolved.
SRI's specific ARPA contract terms for the ARC and NIC work were not found.
